newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - July 16.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - July 16.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) MIDWEEK FRIDAY WEEK AGO
Inland Hem-Fir 417 420 428
Southern Pine Westside 465 460 458
Western Spruce-Pine-Fir 355 359 362

Comment - Despite seasonally strong consumption, ample supplies kept prices of many framing lumber items drifting lower through Tuesday, Random Lengths said in its midweek update. The exception was Southern Pine, where comfortable order files kept mills in control, the lumber reporting agency said.

A plunge at the expiration of CME July futures on Tuesday drew attention away from the cash market. On the labor front, pulp and paper workers began a strike on Monday against three Fletcher Challenge plants in British Columbia.
Trading in structural panels cooled after last week's rally.

Western S-P-F traders' attention focused on the bearish, disorderly expiration of the July futures contract at midday on Tuesday. Speculation about the players was rampant, Random Lengths said. Much of the talk focused on liquidation of a large producer's rumored long position as the driving force at the close. July lumber settled at $356, down $18.50 per tbf.
Western Std&Btr 2x4 was soft but mills were less willing to take counters on #2&Btr items. Selected lengths of #2&Btr proved difficult to cover, and studs were quiet, the agency said.

Eastern S-P-F prices were mostly flat. Some mills took small counters on #1&2 2x4 and 2x6, usually on blocks; 2x8 was off $5-10. Otherwise, retail demand was steady with purchases going heavily to reloads and distributors. Wholesalers bought sparingly except for a few who covered short positions. Prices of dry 2x4 precut studs tumbled $5-10, Random Lengths said.
Southern Pine prices continued to climb. Buyer needs for quick shipments clashed with mill order files of 2-3 weeks.
So Southern Pine quick loads traded as much as $15 higher than comparable tallies two weeks out, led by #2 2x6 and 2x10.

Inland sales of dimesnion and studs were slow, leaving most items vulnerable to counters. A couple of dimension producers shifted production away from Hem-Fir as prices continued to slip. Precut stud prices drifted lower. Ponderosa Pine #2&Btr and #3 1x12 boards continued to erode, Random Lengths said.
Coast Hem-Fir and dry Douglas fir prices drifted sideways to lower. Buyers put off replacing until the last minute, then made the rounds of mills and distributors looking for quick loads.
Coast mills tried to hold quotes steady but were willing to take counters to keep wood moving.

Southern Pine plywood prices were flat as mills had long enough order files to stick to their lists. Some producers reported solid order inquiries but few sales, while others said they booked close to production levels. Secondaries struggled to sell what they owned, the agency said.

Western plywood sheathing and underlayment sales were muted after last week's fast finish. Trading shifted to the secondary level, which offered quicker shipments. Order files extended into next week and the week of July 28. Prices were largely unchanged but a few edged higher. Sanded prices were soft.

OSB prices edged higher in some regions, although follow through from last week's strong finish was muted. Order files ranged from next week to the week of July 28. Some southern mills reported log shortages due to wet weather. Buyers purchased only what they needed to fill inventory holes.
((Chicago newsdesk 312 408 8720))
